articles.title: Logging In
articles.content:
How to Access AureonCare:

**Staff Portal Login:**
1. Navigate to your AureonCare URL
2. Enter your Email Address
3. Enter your Password
4. Click Sign In

**Patient Portal Login:**
1. Navigate to the Patient Portal URL
2. Enter your registered Email Address
3. Enter your Password
4. Click Sign In

**Social Login (OAuth):**
Click one of the social login buttons:
• Sign in with Google
• Sign in with Microsoft
• Sign in with Facebook

Then authorize AureonCare to access your account.

**Forgot Password:**
1. Click 'Forgot Password' on login screen
2. Enter your email address
3. Check email for reset link (valid 1 hour)
4. Click link and create new password
5. Confirm new password
6. Log in with new credentials

**First-Time Login:**
You may be prompted to:
• Change your temporary password
• Set up your user profile
• Upload profile picture (optional)
• Set language preference
• Review assigned roles

**Security Best Practices:**
• Never share your password
• Log out when leaving workstation
• Use unique password for AureonCare
• Report suspicious activity
• Keep contact information current

articles.title: Creating Appointments

Schedule patient appointments quickly and easily

Create appointments from Practice Management module with patient, provider, date, and time selection.

**Accessing Appointment Scheduling:**

1. Go to Practice Management module
2. Click '+ New Appointment' button

Step 1: Select Patient
• Search by name or MRN
• Select from dropdown
• Or click '+ New Patient' to register

Step 2: Choose Provider
• Select from available providers

Step 3: Set Date and Time

Step 4: Appointment Type
• Office Visit
• Telehealth
• Follow-up
• Annual Physical

**After Creating:**
• Appointment appears on calendar

**Calendar Views:**
• Day View - See hourly schedule
• Week View - Plan weekly schedule

• List View - All appointments in list format

**Managing Appointments:**
• Edit - Click appointment to modify
• Cancel - Mark as cancelled with reason
• Reschedule - Change date/time
• Check-in - Mark patient arrived

**Best Practices:**
• Verify patient contact information
• Double-check provider availability

articles.title: Waitlist Management
articles.summary:
NEW IN V1.1: Manage patient waitlist with auto-notifications

Access via Practice Management > Waitlist tab. Set priority levels and automatically notify patients when slots open.
articles.content:
**NEW IN V1.1:** Waitlist now fully integrated into Practice Management!

**Accessing Waitlist:**
1. Go to Practice Management module
2. Click the 'Waitlist' tab (next to List and Calendar)
3. View all patients with status tracking

**Adding Patient to Waitlist:**

**Method 1 - From Appointment Scheduling:**
1. Attempt to schedule appointment
2. If no slots available, click 'Add to Waitlist'
3. Fill in waitlist details
4. Click Save

**Method 2 - Directly from Waitlist Tab:**
1. Go to Practice Management > Waitlist
2. Click '+ Add to Waitlist' button
3. Complete the form
4. Click Save

**Required Fields:**
• Patient (search and select)
• Provider (preferred provider)
• Appointment Type
• Priority (High/Medium/Low)

**Optional Fields:**
• Preferred Date Range
• Preferred Time (Morning/Afternoon/Any)
• Reason for visit
• Internal notes

**Priority Levels:**
🔴 HIGH - Urgent medical need, time-sensitive follow-up (notified first)
🟡 MEDIUM - Standard follow-up, moderately important (notified second)
🟢 LOW - Routine check-up, flexible timing (notified last)

**Status Tracking:**
• Active - Waiting for appointment slot
• Notified - Patient notified of available slot
• Scheduled - Appointment has been scheduled
• Cancelled - Patient no longer needs appointment
• Expired - Patient didn't respond within timeframe

**Auto-Notification System:**
When matching slot becomes available:
1. System identifies matches (provider, type, preferences)
2. Sorts by priority (High > Medium > Low) and date
3. Notifies highest-priority patient via SMS, email, portal
4. Updates status to 'Notified'
5. Patient has 24 hours to confirm

**Confirming Appointments:**
When patient responds 'Yes':
1. Click 'Confirm Appointment' next to entry
2. System automatically creates appointment
3. Updates status to 'Scheduled'
4. Sends confirmation to patient
5. Removes from active waitlist

When patient responds 'No' or doesn't respond:
1. Click 'Move to Next'
2. Original entry marked 'Expired'
3. Next priority patient automatically notified

**Best Practices:**
• Reserve High priority for medically urgent cases
• Document patient preferences in notes
• Review waitlist daily for expired entries
• Call high-priority patients proactively
• Clean up entries older than 30 days
• Verify patient contact information is current

articles.title: Calendar Views
articles.summary:
Switch between different calendar views to manage schedules

Use Day, Week, Month, and List views to visualize and manage appointments efficiently.
articles.content:
**Calendar View Options:**

**Accessing Calendar:**
1. Go to Practice Management module
2. Click 'Calendar' tab
3. Select view type from toolbar

**Available Views:**

**Day View:**
Best for: Detailed daily schedule management

**Features:**
• Hour-by-hour schedule (6 AM - 10 PM)
• 15-minute time increments
• See all providers or filter by specific provider
• Color-coded by appointment type
• Quick click to create appointment at specific time
• Drag-and-drop to reschedule
• See patient names, appointment types, duration
• Blocked time clearly marked

**How to Use:**
1. Click 'Day' button in calendar toolbar
2. Use arrows or date picker to navigate days
3. Click time slot to create new appointment
4. Click existing appointment to view/edit
5. Drag appointment to different time to reschedule

**Week View:**
Best for: Weekly planning and resource allocation

**Features:**
• 7-day spread (Monday-Sunday or custom)
• See multiple providers side-by-side
• Compare schedules across team
• Identify open slots at a glance
• Color-coded appointments
• Shows blocked time and time off

**How to Use:**
1. Click 'Week' button in calendar toolbar
2. Use arrows to navigate weeks
3. Filter by provider or view all
4. Click any time slot to create appointment
5. Scroll horizontally to see more providers

**Month View:**
Best for: Long-term planning and overview

**Features:**
• Full month calendar grid
• See appointment counts per day
• Color indicators for busy/light days
• Holidays and time off displayed
• Recurring appointments visible
• Quick navigation between months

**How to Use:**
1. Click 'Month' button in calendar toolbar
2. Use arrows or month picker to navigate
3. Click date to see day's appointments
4. Hover over date to see appointment preview
5. Click date to switch to Day view for that date

**Day Count Indicators:**
• Green - Light (0-5 appointments)
• Yellow - Moderate (6-12 appointments)
• Orange - Busy (13-18 appointments)
• Red - Very Busy (19+ appointments)

**List View:**
Best for: Searching, sorting, and bulk operations

**Features:**
• Table format with sortable columns
• Advanced filters and search
• Bulk actions (cancel, reschedule)
• Export to CSV/Excel
• See upcoming appointments chronologically
• Filter by status, provider, patient, type

**Columns:**
• Date & Time
• Patient Name & MRN
• Provider
• Appointment Type
• Duration
• Status
• Location (if multi-site)
• Actions (View, Edit, Cancel)

**How to Use:**
1. Click 'List' button in calendar toolbar
2. Use search box to find appointments
3. Click column headers to sort
4. Apply filters from dropdown menus
5. Select multiple appointments for bulk actions
6. Click Export to download list

**Filtering Options:**

**Filter by Provider:**
1. Click provider filter dropdown
2. Select specific provider(s)
3. Or choose 'All Providers'

**Filter by Status:**
• Scheduled - Confirmed appointments
• Confirmed - Patient confirmed attendance
• Checked In - Patient arrived
• In Progress - Currently being seen
• Completed - Visit finished
• No Show - Patient didn't arrive
• Cancelled - Appointment cancelled

**Filter by Type:**
• Office Visit
• Telehealth
• Follow-up
• Annual Physical
• Procedure
• Consultation
• Custom types

**Filter by Date Range:**
1. Click date range selector
2. Choose preset:
   • Today
   • This Week
   • This Month
   • Next 7 Days
   • Next 30 Days
3. Or select custom date range

**Color Coding System:**

**By Appointment Type:**
• Blue - Office Visit
• Purple - Telehealth
• Green - Follow-up
• Orange - Annual Physical
• Red - Urgent/Same-Day
• Gray - Cancelled
• Custom colors for custom types

**By Status:**
• Solid fill - Scheduled/Confirmed
• Striped - Tentative/Unconfirmed
• Faded - Completed
• Red border - No Show
• Crosshatch - Cancelled

**Calendar Actions:**

**Creating Appointment:**
1. Click any open time slot
2. 'New Appointment' modal opens
3. Pre-filled with date/time/provider
4. Complete form and save

**Editing Appointment:**
1. Click existing appointment
2. Appointment details modal opens
3. Click 'Edit' button
4. Modify details and save

**Rescheduling:**
**Method 1 - Drag and Drop:**
1. Click and hold appointment
2. Drag to new time slot
3. Release to drop
4. Confirm new time

**Method 2 - Edit:**
1. Click appointment
2. Click 'Reschedule'
3. Select new date/time
4. Save changes

**Cancelling:**
1. Click appointment
2. Click 'Cancel' button
3. Select cancellation reason
4. Add notes (optional)
5. Notify patient (optional)
6. Confirm cancellation

**Quick Actions:**
• Check In - Mark patient arrived
• No Show - Mark patient didn't arrive
• Complete - Mark visit completed
• Print - Print appointment card
• SMS - Send reminder to patient

**Calendar Settings:**

**Time Range:**
1. Click settings gear icon
2. Set start time (default 6 AM)
3. Set end time (default 10 PM)
4. Save preferences

**Time Increments:**
Choose slot duration:
• 10 minutes
• 15 minutes (default)
• 30 minutes
• 60 minutes

**Default View:**
Set which view opens by default:
• Day
• Week
• Month
• List

**Weekend Display:**
Toggle Saturday/Sunday visibility

**Keyboard Shortcuts:**
• Arrow Keys - Navigate days/weeks
• T - Jump to Today
• D - Switch to Day view
• W - Switch to Week view
• M - Switch to Month view
• L - Switch to List view
• N - Create new appointment
• / - Focus search box

**Printing Calendar:**
1. Click Print icon in toolbar
2. Select view to print
3. Choose date range
4. Select providers to include
5. Preview and print

**Best Practices:**
• Use Day view for detailed daily management
• Use Week view for team coordination
• Use Month view for planning ahead
• Use List view for searching and reporting
• Color-code appointment types consistently
• Review calendar daily for gaps or conflicts
• Block lunch and administrative time
• Set realistic appointment durations
• Keep calendar up-to-date with cancellations

articles.title: Provider Scheduling
articles.summary:
Manage provider availability and working hours

Set up provider schedules, block time for meetings or procedures, and manage time-off requests.
articles.content:
**Managing Provider Schedules:**

**Accessing Provider Scheduling:**
1. Go to Administration > Providers
2. Select a provider
3. Click 'Manage Schedule' tab
4. Or go to Practice Management > Provider Schedules

**Setting Up Provider Availability:**

**Regular Working Hours:**
1. Click 'Set Schedule' button
2. For each day of week:
   • Toggle working day on/off
   • Set start time (e.g., 8:00 AM)
   • Set end time (e.g., 5:00 PM)
   • Add lunch break (optional)
   • Add multiple time blocks per day

**Example Schedule:**
Monday - Friday:
• 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM (Morning)
• 12:00 PM - 1:00 PM (Lunch - Blocked)
• 1:00 PM - 5:00 PM (Afternoon)

Saturday:
• 9:00 AM - 1:00 PM (Half day)

Sunday:
• Closed

**Appointment Slot Configuration:**

**Default Slot Duration:**
• 15 minutes - Quick follow-ups
• 30 minutes - Standard office visits
• 45 minutes - New patient visits
• 60 minutes - Physicals, consultations

**Buffer Time:**
• Between appointments (5-10 min)
• Prevents back-to-back scheduling
• Allows for charting/documentation
• Accounts for running late

**Appointment Types by Duration:**
1. Click 'Appointment Types'
2. Set custom duration for each type:
   • Office Visit: 30 min
   • Annual Physical: 60 min
   • Follow-up: 15 min
   • Procedure: varies
   • Telehealth: 20 min

**Blocking Time:**

**One-Time Blocks:**
1. Go to provider's calendar
2. Click time slot to block
3. Select 'Block Time'
4. Choose reason:
   • Meeting/Conference
   • Procedure/Surgery
   • Administrative Time
   • Training
   • Personal
5. Set start and end time
6. Add notes (optional)
7. Click 'Save Block'

**Recurring Blocks:**
For regular commitments:
1. Click 'Create Recurring Block'
2. Set schedule:
   • Every Tuesday 2:00-3:00 PM
   • First Monday of month
   • Every other Wednesday
3. Set recurrence pattern:
   • Daily
   • Weekly (select days)
   • Monthly (select date or day)
   • Custom
4. Set end date or number of occurrences
5. Reason and notes
6. Save

**Common Recurring Blocks:**
• Weekly staff meetings
• Monthly quality review
• Thursday afternoon procedures
• Every other Friday administrative time

**Time Off Management:**

**Requesting Time Off:**
1. Go to My Schedule > Request Time Off
2. Select type:
   • Vacation
   • Sick Leave
   • Conference/CME
   • Personal Day
   • Holiday
3. Select date range
4. Add notes/justification
5. Submit request

**Approving Time Off (Admins):**
1. Go to Administration > Time Off Requests
2. Review pending requests
3. Check coverage for dates
4. Approve or deny with notes
5. System blocks calendar automatically
6. Notifies provider of decision

**When Time Off Approved:**
• Calendar blocked for date range
• Existing appointments flagged for rescheduling
• New appointments prevented during period
• Out-of-office message can be set
• Coverage provider assigned (optional)

**Coverage Providers:**

**Assigning Coverage:**
When provider is out:
1. Set time off period
2. Click 'Assign Coverage'
3. Select covering provider(s)
4. Set rules:
   • Transfer all appointments
   • Only urgent/same-day
   • By appointment type
5. Notify patients of change (optional)
6. Existing appointments updated

**Multiple Locations:**

If provider works at multiple locations:
1. Go to Provider > Locations
2. Add each location
3. Set schedule per location:
   • Monday/Wednesday - Main Office
   • Tuesday/Thursday - Satellite Clinic
   • Friday - Hospital Rounds
4. Calendar shows location for each slot
5. Appointments automatically tagged with location

**Appointment Limits:**

**Daily Limits:**
Prevent overbooking:
1. Set max appointments per day
2. Set max new patients per day
3. Set max specific appointment types
4. System warns when approaching limit
5. Admin override available if needed

**Example Limits:**
• Max 20 appointments/day
• Max 4 new patients/day
• Max 2 annual physicals/day
• Max 5 telehealth visits/day

**Emergency/ASAP Slots:**

**Reserved Slots:**
1. Block specific slots daily for urgent visits
2. Example: 11:00 AM and 3:00 PM
3. Only bookable as 'Urgent' or 'Same-Day'
4. Auto-released if not used by cutoff time
5. Cutoff: 2 hours before slot time

**Override Scheduling:**

**Double Booking:**
For emergencies/urgent needs:
1. Attempt to book filled slot
2. System shows conflict warning
3. Select 'Override - Urgent'
4. Add justification
5. Provider notified of double-book
6. Appears as overlapping on calendar

**Outside Working Hours:**
1. Attempt to book blocked time
2. System warns 'Outside working hours'
3. Admin can override
4. Provider notified
5. Requires approval if provider settings require it

**Schedule Templates:**

**Creating Templates:**
1. Set up ideal weekly schedule
2. Include:
   • Working hours
   • Blocked time
   • Appointment types distribution
   • Buffer times
3. Save as template
4. Apply to future weeks with one click

**Template Use Cases:**
• Seasonal schedules (summer vs winter)
• Rotating schedules
• New provider onboarding
• Standardizing across providers

**Schedule Reports:**

**Available Reports:**
• Provider utilization (% of time booked)
• No-show rate by provider
• Average appointment duration
• Peak appointment times
• Cancellation patterns
• Time off summary
• Revenue per provider hour

**Best Practices:**
• Set realistic appointment durations
• Build in buffer time for documentation
• Reserve slots for urgent/same-day
• Review and update schedule quarterly
• Communicate schedule changes in advance
• Use templates for consistency
• Monitor utilization to optimize
• Block administrative time for charting
• Coordinate time off with colleagues
• Set automatic lunch blocks
• Review no-shows and adjust overbooking
• Use recurring blocks for standing commitments
• Assign coverage for all absences
• Keep contact info current for notifications

articles.title: Patient Registration
articles.summary:
Register new patients and set up portal access

Enter demographics, insurance, emergency contacts, and enable patient portal for online access.
articles.content:
**Registering New Patients:**

**Accessing Registration:**
1. Go to Patients module
2. Click '+ New Patient' button
3. Or click 'Add New Patient' from dashboard

**Registration Process - 5 Steps:**

**STEP 1: Demographics**

**Required Fields:**
• First Name
• Last Name
• Date of Birth
• Gender (Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say)
• Phone Number (primary contact)
• Email Address

**Optional Fields:**
• Middle Name
• Preferred Name (what patient likes to be called)
• Suffix (Jr., Sr., III)
• SSN (last 4 digits or full, encrypted)
• Language Preference
• Race/Ethnicity (for reporting)
• Marital Status
• Occupation

**Address Information:**
• Street Address
• Apartment/Unit Number
• City
• State/Province
• ZIP/Postal Code
• Country

**Additional Contact:**
• Secondary Phone (mobile/work)
• Preferred Contact Method (Phone, Email, SMS, Portal)
• Best Time to Call

**STEP 2: Insurance Information**

**Primary Insurance:**
• Insurance Company (search from list or add new)
• Policy/Member ID Number
• Group Number
• Policy Holder Name (if different from patient)
• Policy Holder DOB
• Relationship to Patient (Self, Spouse, Parent, Other)
• Effective Date
• Upload Insurance Card:
  - Front (required)
  - Back (required)

**Secondary Insurance (Optional):**
Same fields as primary insurance

**Insurance Verification:**
1. Click 'Verify Coverage' button
2. System checks eligibility in real-time
3. Displays:
   • Active/Inactive status
   • Copay amount
   • Deductible status
   • Coverage details

**STEP 3: Emergency Contact**

**Primary Emergency Contact:**
• Full Name
• Relationship to Patient
• Phone Number (home)
• Mobile Phone
• Email Address
• Address (if different from patient)

**Secondary Emergency Contact (Optional):**
Same fields as primary contact

**STEP 4: Medical History (Optional)**

Can be completed now or during first visit:
• Allergies
• Current Medications
• Past Medical History
• Family History
• Social History
• Surgical History

**STEP 5: Portal Access**

**Enable Patient Portal:**
1. Toggle 'Enable Portal Access'
2. Patient receives email invitation
3. Email contains:
   • Portal URL
   • Temporary password or setup link
   • Instructions for first login

**Portal Features:**
• View medical records
• Schedule appointments
• Request prescription refills
• Message providers
• View test results
• Pay bills online
• Update personal information

**Portal Setup Options:**
• Send invitation immediately
• Send invitation later
• Generate temporary password
• Require patient to set password on first login

**Completing Registration:**

1. Review all information
2. Click 'Save Patient' button
3. System generates:
   • MRN (Medical Record Number) - auto-assigned
   • Patient ID
   • Chart number
4. Patient added to system
5. Portal invitation sent (if enabled)

**After Registration:**

**Immediate Actions:**
• Schedule first appointment
• Add to waitlist if no availability
• Collect copay/payment
• Scan insurance cards
• Provide new patient forms
• Give office policies handout

**Patient Chart Created:**
• Empty chart ready for documentation
• Demographics populated
• Insurance information loaded
• Portal access configured
• Ready for clinical use

**Quick Registration (Walk-In):**

For urgent/walk-in patients:
1. Click 'Quick Registration'
2. Minimal fields required:
   • Name
   • Date of Birth
   • Phone Number
3. Complete full registration later
4. System flags chart as 'Incomplete'

**Duplicate Detection:**

System checks for duplicates based on:
• First Name + Last Name + DOB
• SSN (if provided)
• Phone Number + DOB

If potential duplicate found:
1. System displays warning
2. Shows matching patient(s)
3. Options:
   • Continue with new registration
   • Link to existing patient
   • Cancel registration

**Required Documents:**

**To Collect:**
• Photo ID (driver's license, passport)
• Insurance card(s) - front and back
• Referral (if required by insurance)
• Previous medical records (if transferring)

**To Provide:**
• HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices
• Patient Rights and Responsibilities
• Financial Policy
• Office Policies
• Portal registration instructions
• New patient forms (if not pre-filled)

**Minor Patients (Under 18):**

**Additional Requirements:**
• Parent/Guardian information
• Parent/Guardian ID and signature
• Custody documentation (if applicable)
• Insurance through parent/guardian

**Portal Access for Minors:**
• Age 13-17: Parent proxy access with patient view
• Under 13: Parent-only access
• State-specific rules may apply

**Special Populations:**

**Medicare Patients:**
• Verify Medicare number
• Check Part A/B/D coverage
• Capture Medicare card image
• Document Advanced Beneficiary Notice (ABN) consent

**Medicaid Patients:**
• Verify active coverage monthly
• Some states require re-verification
• Check managed care plan

**Self-Pay/Uninsured:**
• Discuss payment options
• Offer payment plans
• Provide cash discount if applicable
• Document financial agreement

**Updating Patient Information:**

**At Each Visit:**
Verify and update:
• Address and phone number
• Insurance coverage
• Emergency contacts
• Medications and allergies
• Employer (if relevant)

**To Update:**
1. Open patient chart
2. Click 'Edit Demographics'
3. Update changed fields
4. Save changes
5. System logs who made changes and when

**Best Practices:**
• Verify insurance before every visit
• Scan all documents (ID, insurance cards)
• Enable portal access for all eligible patients
• Complete registration fully before first visit
• Review patient information at check-in
• Use duplicate detection to avoid duplicates
• Document any special needs or accommodations
• Update pharmacy preferences
• Verify consent for electronic communications
• Keep emergency contacts current

articles.title: Searching Patients
articles.summary:
Find patients quickly using advanced search and filters

Search by name, MRN, phone, date of birth, or use advanced filters to locate patient records.
articles.content:
**Patient Search Methods:**

**Quick Search:**

**Global Search Bar:**
Available from any page:
1. Click search icon in top toolbar
2. Or press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac)
3. Type search query
4. Results appear instantly

**Search Criteria:**
Search supports:
• Patient name (first, last, or both)
• MRN (Medical Record Number)
• Phone number
• Date of Birth
• Email address
• SSN (last 4 digits)

**Examples:**
• "John Smith" - Finds all John Smiths
• "Smith, John" - Same, different format
• "MRN12345" - Finds by MRN
• "555-1234" - Finds by phone (partial OK)
• "01/15/1980" - Finds by DOB

**From Patients Module:**

**Basic Search:**
1. Go to Patients module
2. Use search box at top of patient list
3. Type name, MRN, or phone
4. List filters in real-time
5. Click patient to open chart

**Search Tips:**
• Partial names work ("Joh" finds "John")
• Not case-sensitive
• Ignores special characters in phone numbers
• Searches all fields simultaneously
• Results sorted by relevance

**Advanced Search:**

**Accessing Advanced Search:**
1. Go to Patients module
2. Click 'Advanced Search' or filter icon
3. Advanced search panel opens

**Filter Options:**

**Demographics:**
• Age Range (e.g., 18-65)
• Gender (Male, Female, Other, All)
• Date of Birth range
• City/State/ZIP Code
• Language Preference

**Clinical:**
• Primary Diagnosis (ICD-10 code)
• Active Medications
• Allergies (specific allergen)
• Active Problems
• Last Visit Date range
• Provider (primary or any)

**Insurance:**
• Insurance Company
• Insurance Type (Commercial, Medicare, Medicaid, Self-Pay)
• Coverage Status (Active, Inactive, Pending)
• Policy expiration date

**Status:**
• Active Patients
• Inactive Patients (not seen in 2+ years)
• Deceased
• Portal Enabled/Disabled
• Outstanding Balance

**Appointment Related:**
• Upcoming Appointments
• No appointments scheduled
• No-show history
• Cancelled appointments
• Missed annual physical

**Custom Filters:**
• Patient Tags/Labels
• Custom Fields
• Risk Scores
• Care Programs enrolled

**Multiple Filter Combinations:**
Stack filters for precise results:

**Example 1 - Diabetic Patients Due for A1C:**
• Diagnosis: Diabetes (E11.9)
• Last A1C: >90 days ago
• Active patients only

**Example 2 - Medicare Annual Wellness Visit Due:**
• Insurance: Medicare
• Age: 65+
• Last AWV: >12 months ago

**Example 3 - Overdue Follow-ups:**
• Last Visit: >6 months ago
• Has chronic condition
• Active patients
• Outstanding balance = No

**Saved Searches:**

**Creating Saved Search:**
1. Set up advanced filters
2. Click 'Save Search'
3. Name the search (e.g., "Diabetics Due for Labs")
4. Save

**Using Saved Searches:**
1. Click 'Saved Searches' dropdown
2. Select saved search
3. Filters auto-apply
4. Results display immediately

**Common Saved Searches:**
• Active Diabetics
• Medicare Patients

articles.title: Medical Records
articles.summary:
Create and manage electronic health records and clinical notes

Document patient encounters using SOAP notes, templates, and structured charting tools.
articles.content:
**Electronic Health Records (EHR):**

**Accessing Patient Chart:**
1. Search for patient (Ctrl+K)
2. Click patient name from results
3. Or go to Patients module > Select patient
4. Patient chart opens

**Chart Sections:**

**Summary Tab:**
• Vital Signs (most recent)
• Active Problems/Diagnoses
• Current Medications
• Allergies
• Recent Visits
• Upcoming Appointments
• Active Lab Orders
• Care Team

**Progress Notes Tab:**
• All clinical documentation
• Visit notes
• Phone encounters
• Telehealth notes
• Procedure notes

**Medications Tab:**
• Active Prescriptions
• Discontinued Medications
• Medication History
• Prescription Requests

**Laboratory Tab:**
• Pending Orders
• Results (with abnormal flags)
• Lab History
• Trending/Graphs

**Imaging Tab:**
• Radiology Orders
• Reports
• Images (DICOM viewer)

**Documents Tab:**
• Uploaded Documents
• Scanned Records
• External Records
• Consent Forms

**Creating Clinical Notes:**

**Starting a New Note:**
1. Open patient chart
2. Click 'Progress Notes' tab
3. Click '+ New Note' button
4. Select note type

**Note Types:**
• Office Visit
• Annual Physical
• Follow-up Visit
• Urgent Care
• Telehealth
• Phone Encounter
• Procedure Note
• Letter/Referral
• Hospital Consultation
• Custom Types

**SOAP Note Format:**

Most common structure:

**Subjective (S):**
Patient's reported symptoms/concerns
• Chief Complaint
• History of Present Illness (HPI)
• Review of Systems (ROS)
• Past Medical/Surgical/Family/Social History

**Objective (O):**
Measurable findings
• Vital Signs:
  - Blood Pressure
  - Heart Rate
  - Temperature
  - Respiratory Rate
  - Oxygen Saturation
  - Height/Weight/BMI
• Physical Examination:
  - General Appearance
  - HEENT (Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, Throat)
  - Cardiovascular
  - Respiratory
  - Abdomen
  - Extremities
  - Neurological
  - Skin
• Test Results (labs, imaging)

**Assessment (A):**
Provider's clinical impression
• List of diagnoses (with ICD-10 codes)
• Problem status (new, stable, worsening, resolved)
• Differential diagnoses

**Plan (P):**
Treatment and follow-up
• Medications (new, modified, discontinued)
• Lab orders
• Imaging orders
• Referrals
• Patient education
• Follow-up appointment timeframe
• Return precautions

**Documentation Tools:**

**Templates:**
1. Click 'Templates' button
2. Browse by specialty or type
3. Select template
4. Auto-populates note sections
5. Customize as needed

**Common Templates:**
• Annual Physical
• Diabetes Follow-up
• Hypertension Management
• Well-Child Visit
• Sports Physical
• Post-Operative Visit
• Pre-Op Clearance

**Macros/SmartPhrases:**
Reusable text snippets

**How to Use:**
1. Type macro shortcut (e.g., ".normal_neuro")
2. Expands to full text
3. Edit as needed

**Examples:**
• .ros = Full Review of Systems template
• .pe = Physical Exam template
• .dm = Diabetes management plan
• .htn = Hypertension management plan

**Voice Dictation:**
1. Click microphone icon
2. Speak clearly
3. System transcribes in real-time
4. Edit for accuracy
5. Medical terminology recognized

**Copy Forward:**
Bring forward previous note elements:
1. Click 'Copy From Previous'
2. Select which sections to copy:
   • Past Medical History
   • Medications
   • Allergies
   • Social History
   • Review of Systems
3. Update changed information

**Vital Signs Entry:**

**Recording Vitals:**
1. In note or separate vitals section
2. Enter measurements:
   • BP: 120/80 mmHg
   • HR: 72 bpm
   • Temp: 98.6°F (37°C)
   • RR: 16 breaths/min
   • O2 Sat: 98%
   • Height: 5'10" (178 cm)
   • Weight: 170 lbs (77 kg)
   • BMI: Auto-calculated
3. Add time and location
4. Save

**Vital Signs Display:**
• Color-coded for abnormal values
• Trending graphs available
• Comparison to previous visits
• Alerts for critical values

**Adding Diagnoses:**

**From Assessment Section:**
1. Type diagnosis or ICD-10 code
2. Search dropdown appears
3. Select correct diagnosis
4. Set status:
   • Active
   • Chronic
   • Resolved
   • Rule Out
5. Set date of onset
6. Add to problem list

**Problem List Management:**
• Active Problems - Currently being treated
• Chronic Problems - Ongoing conditions
• Past Problems - Resolved/Inactive
• Mark primary diagnosis for visit
• Link to prescriptions and orders

**Ordering from Note:**

**Lab Orders:**
1. In Plan section, click 'Order Labs'
2. Select tests
3. Auto-linked to current diagnosis
4. Order details pre-filled

**Prescriptions:**
1. Click 'Prescribe'
2. ePrescribe workflow opens
3. Diagnosis from note auto-populated
4. Complete and send

**Referrals:**
1. Click 'Refer'
2. Select specialist/facility
3. Reason pre-filled from note
4. Generate referral letter

**Completing the Note:**

**Review:**
1. Review all sections for completeness
2. Check spelling and grammar
3. Verify diagnoses coded correctly
4. Ensure orders placed

**Sign and Lock:**
1. Click 'Sign Note'
2. Apply electronic signature
3. Note becomes part of legal record
4. Cannot be edited (only addendums allowed)

**If Not Ready to Sign:**
• Save as Draft
• Returns to note later
• Marked as 'Unsigned' in note list

**Addendums:**

For signed notes requiring changes:
1. Open signed note
2. Click 'Add Addendum'
3. Enter additional information
4. Cannot modify original text
5. Addendum timestamped and signed separately

**Co-Signing:**

For supervised providers:
1. Resident/Student creates note
2. Clicks 'Request Co-Signature'
3. Attending receives notification
4. Attending reviews and co-signs
5. Both signatures on record

**Document Scanning:**

**Uploading External Documents:**
1. Click 'Documents' tab
2. Click 'Upload'
3. Select file (PDF, JPG, PNG)
4. Categorize:
   • Consent Forms
   • External Records
   • Lab Reports
   • Imaging Reports
   • Correspondence
5. Add date and description
6. Save

**Best Practices:**
• Sign notes same day as visit
• Use templates for consistency
• Link diagnoses to orders and prescriptions
• Document patient education provided
• Include time spent (for billing)
• Use specific, objective language
• Avoid copy-paste errors
• Review before signing
• Document phone calls and portal messages
• Update problem list regularly
• Record medication reconciliation
• Note patient adherence/non-adherence
• Include patient's understanding of plan
• Document informed consent for procedures

articles.title: Prescriptions & ePrescribe
articles.summary:
NEW IN V1.1: ePrescribe with edit mode and diagnosis linking

4-step workflow: Search medication, enter details, select pharmacy, review and submit with drug interaction checking.
articles.content:
**NEW IN V1.1:** Edit mode now prefills medication name with step-by-step workflow!

**Accessing ePrescribe:**

**From Patient Chart:**
1. Open patient's chart
2. Go to 'Medications' tab
3. Click '+ New Prescription' button
4. ePrescribe modal opens with 4-step workflow

**From Clinical Encounter:**
1. During patient visit/clinical note
2. Click 'Prescribe Medication' in toolbar
3. Patient context pre-loaded

**4-Step Workflow:**

**STEP 1: Search Medication**
1. Type medication name or NDC code
2. Select specific drug formulation:
   • Brand name or generic
   • Strength (10mg, 20mg, etc.)
   • Form (tablet, capsule, liquid)
3. Review drug information
4. Click 'Next'

**NEW:** In edit mode, medication name is prefilled - skip search!

**STEP 2: Prescription Details**
Enter:
• Dosage (strength and quantity per dose)
• Frequency (once daily, twice daily, every 6 hours)
• Route (oral, topical, IV, IM)
• Duration (7 days, 30 days, until finished)
• Quantity (total number to dispense)
• Refills (0, 1, 2, 3, PRN)
• Instructions (patient-facing SIG directions)
• Notes (internal clinical notes)

**Special Options:**
• Generic Substitution toggle (DAW)
• Prior Authorization checkbox
• Controlled Substance auto-flagged

**STEP 3: Select Pharmacy**
1. Patient's preferred pharmacy pre-selected
2. Search by name, address, or zip code
3. Choose from recent pharmacies
4. Add new pharmacy if needed

**STEP 4: Review and Submit**
1. Review all information:
   • Patient demographics and allergies
   • Medication details and instructions
   • Pharmacy information
   • Drug interactions and warnings

2. **NEW:** Link to Diagnosis
   • Select primary diagnosis for prescription
   • Links to ICD-10 code for insurance
   • Improves claim approval rates

3. Apply digital signature
4. Click 'Submit Prescription'

**Drug Interaction Checking:**
🔴 CRITICAL - Severe interaction, prescription blocked (override required)
🟡 MODERATE - Potential interaction, warning displayed
🟢 MINOR - Low-risk interaction, informational
⚠️ ALLERGY - Patient allergic, blocked (override with justification)
👶 AGE - Not recommended for age, warning
🤰 PREGNANCY - Contraindicated in pregnancy

**Editing Existing Prescriptions:**
1. Go to Patient Chart > Medications
2. Find prescription in active list
3. Click 'Edit' icon
4. **NEW:** Medication name prefilled (can't change drug)
5. Update dosage, frequency, quantity, instructions
6. Navigate between steps with context maintained
7. Click 'Update Prescription'

**Managing Prescriptions:**

**Renewing:**
1. Click 'Renew' next to prescription
2. Review and update if needed
3. Update refill count and quantity
4. Submit renewed prescription

**Discontinuing:**
1. Click 'Discontinue'
2. Select reason (completed, adverse reaction, no longer needed)
3. Add optional notes
4. Confirm discontinuation

**Status Tracking:**
• Pending - Submitted, not processed by pharmacy
• Sent - Transmitted to pharmacy
• Received - Pharmacy acknowledged
• Filled - Pharmacy filled prescription
• Picked Up - Patient picked up medication
• Error - Transmission failed, resubmit
• Cancelled - Prescription cancelled

**Controlled Substances (EPCS):**
• Valid DEA number required
• Two-factor authentication for each CS prescription
• State-specific rules apply
• No refills for Schedule II

**Best Practices:**
• Always review allergies before prescribing
• Link prescriptions to diagnoses
• Write clear, patient-friendly instructions
• Never ignore drug interaction warnings
• Verify pharmacy selection
• Document alert overrides
• Keep medication list current
• Check prescription status

articles.title: Diagnosis Management
articles.summary:
Manage patient diagnoses and problem lists with ICD-10 codes

Add, update, and link diagnoses to prescriptions, lab orders, and claims for proper documentation.
articles.content:
**Managing Patient Diagnoses:**

**Accessing Diagnoses:**
1. Open patient chart
2. Click 'Problems' or 'Diagnoses' tab
3. View active and past diagnoses

**Problem List Overview:**

**Active Problems:**
Conditions currently being treated or monitored
• Chronic diseases (Diabetes, Hypertension)
• Acute conditions (Infections, injuries)
• Ongoing issues requiring management

**Chronic Problems:**
Long-term conditions (subset of active)
• Marked separately for easy identification
• Typically require ongoing medication
• Need regular monitoring

**Past/Resolved Problems:**
• Previously active, now resolved
• Kept for historical reference
• Not shown in active problem list
• Available in medical history

**Adding New Diagnosis:**

**Method 1 - From Problem List:**
1. Open patient chart
2. Go to 'Problems' tab
3. Click '+ Add Diagnosis'
4. Search for diagnosis

**Method 2 - From Clinical Note:**
1. In SOAP note Assessment section
2. Type diagnosis name or code
3. Select from dropdown
4. Automatically added to problem list

**Method 3 - From Prescription:**
1. When prescribing medication
2. Step 4: Link to diagnosis
3. Can add new diagnosis on-the-fly

**Searching for Diagnoses:**

**ICD-10 Code Search:**
Multiple search methods:

**By Description:**
• Type: "diabetes"
• Shows all diabetes-related codes:
  - E11.9 - Type 2 Diabetes without complications
  - E11.65 - Type 2 Diabetes with hyperglycemia
  - E10.9 - Type 1 Diabetes
  - E11.22 - Type 2 Diabetes with chronic kidney disease

**By ICD-10 Code:**
• Type: "E11.9"
• Direct match displayed
• Related codes suggested

**By Body System:**
• Browse categories:
  - Endocrine (E codes)
  - Circulatory (I codes)
  - Respiratory (J codes)
  - Digestive (K codes)
  - Musculoskeletal (M codes)

**Smart Search Features:**
• Autocomplete as you type
• Shows code + description
• Recently used codes at top
• Favorite/common codes saved
• Synonym recognition ("sugar diabetes" = diabetes mellitus)

**Diagnosis Details:**

**Required Fields:**
• ICD-10 Code (e.g., E11.9)
• Description (auto-filled from code)
• Date of Onset
• Status (Active, Chronic, Resolved)

**Optional Fields:**
• Severity (Mild, Moderate, Severe)
• Laterality (Left, Right, Bilateral) - if applicable
• Stage/Grade (for cancers, ulcers, etc.)
• Clinical Notes
• Treating Provider
• Date Resolved (if applicable)

**Status Types:**

**Active:**
Currently being treated
• Shows in active problem list
• Included in encounter documentation
• Available for linking to orders/prescriptions

**Chronic:**
Ongoing, long-term condition
• Subset of Active
• Flagged for special tracking
• Requires regular monitoring
• Examples: Diabetes, Hypertension, Asthma

**Resolved:**
No longer active
• Moves to past medical history
• Not in active problem list
• Available for reference
• Date resolved documented

**Rule Out:**
Differential diagnosis, not confirmed
• Appears with "R/O" prefix
• Used during workup
• Update to Active or Remove after testing

**Linking Diagnoses:**

**Link to Prescriptions:**

When prescribing medication:
1. ePrescribe Step 4
2. Select primary diagnosis for prescription
3. Improves claim approval
4. Documents medical necessity

**Example:**
Prescribing Metformin → Link to E11.9 (Type 2 Diabetes)

**Link to Lab Orders:**

When ordering labs:
1. Step 1: Clinical Indication required
2. Select diagnosis from problem list
3. Links order to condition
4. Supports medical necessity

**Example:**
Ordering A1C → Link to E11.9 (Type 2 Diabetes)

**Link to Procedures:**

For procedures and billing:
1. Procedure requires diagnosis pointer
2. Select applicable diagnosis(es)
3. Up to 12 diagnoses per claim
4. Primary diagnosis listed first

**Link to Encounters:**

In clinical note:
1. Assessment section lists diagnoses
2. Mark primary diagnosis for visit
3. Links to E&M code for billing
4. Supports level of service billed

**Managing Existing Diagnoses:**

**Editing:**
1. Click diagnosis in problem list
2. Click 'Edit'
3. Update fields:
   • Change status
   • Update severity
   • Add notes
   • Modify date
4. Save changes

**Resolving:**
1. Click diagnosis
2. Click 'Mark as Resolved'
3. Enter resolution date
4. Add resolution notes (optional)
5. Moves to past medical history

**Deleting:**
Only if added in error:
1. Click diagnosis
2. Click 'Delete'
3. Confirm deletion
4. Provide reason
5. Permanently removed (logged in audit trail)

**Problem List Best Practices:**

**Keep it Current:**
• Review at every visit
• Resolve conditions that are inactive
• Update status as conditions change
• Remove duplicate entries

**Be Specific:**
• Use most specific ICD-10 code available
• E11.65 (with hyperglycemia) vs E11.9 (unspecified)
• Include laterality when relevant
• Document stage/severity

**Prioritize:**
• List most significant problems first
• Mark chronic conditions clearly
• Identify primary diagnosis for visit

**Link Everything:**
• Link prescriptions to diagnoses
• Link lab orders to diagnoses
• Link procedures to diagnoses
• Improves claims approval
• Documents medical necessity

**Common Diagnosis Scenarios:**

**Multiple Related Diagnoses:**

Example - Diabetes complications:
• E11.9 - Type 2 Diabetes (primary)
• E11.22 - Type 2 Diabetes with CKD (if kidney disease present)
• E11.36 - Type 2 Diabetes with diabetic neuropathy
• E11.319 - Type 2 Diabetes with diabetic retinopathy

Keep all relevant codes active for comprehensive documentation.

**Combination Codes:**

Some conditions have single combined codes:
• I10 - Essential Hypertension (use instead of separate codes)
• J44.0 - COPD with acute lower respiratory infection (not COPD + pneumonia separately)

Use combination code when available.

**Diagnosis Hierarchy:**

For claims and documentation:
1. Primary Diagnosis - Main reason for visit/service
2. Secondary Diagnoses - Contributing factors
3. Additional Diagnoses - Other relevant conditions

**Quality Measures:**

Certain diagnoses trigger quality reporting:
• Diabetes → A1C testing required
• Hypertension → BP control monitoring
• COPD → Spirometry testing
• Depression → PHQ-9 screening

System flags these for compliance tracking.

**Diagnosis Reports:**

**Available Reports:**
• Active Diagnoses by Patient
• Diagnosis Frequency (most common)
• Chronic Disease Registry
• Quality Measure Compliance
• Diagnosis by Provider
• Missing Diagnosis Links (prescriptions without diagnosis)

**Using Reports:**
1. Go to Reports module
2. Select 'Diagnosis Reports'
3. Choose report type
4. Set filters (date range, provider, diagnosis)
5. Generate and export

**ICD-10 Code Updates:**

**Annual Updates:**
October 1st each year:
• New codes added
• Some codes deleted
• Descriptions modified
• System auto-updates

**When Code Changes:**
• System notifies affected charts
• Recommend updating to new code
• Old code still visible in history
• Update prospectively, not retrospectively

**Best Practices:**
• Use most specific code possible (5-6 characters)
• Include laterality when applicable (right vs left)
• Document stage/severity for cancers
• Link all prescriptions to diagnoses
• Keep problem list current and accurate
• Resolve inactive problems
• Use chronic designation appropriately
• Review problem list at each visit
• Verify diagnoses support procedures/tests ordered
• Use combination codes when available
• Don't use unspecified codes if more specific available
• Document onset dates accurately
• Include patient in problem list review
• Use consistent terminology
• Avoid outdated or obsolete codes

articles.title: Laboratory Orders
articles.summary:
NEW IN V1.1: Order labs with CPT multiselect and recurring orders

Select from 80+ tests organized by category. Support for one-time, recurring, and future scheduled orders.
articles.content:
**NEW IN V1.1:** CPT multiselect (80+ tests), recurring orders, and enhanced print functionality!

**Accessing Lab Orders:**

**From Patient Chart:**
1. Open patient's chart
2. Go to 'Laboratory' tab
3. Click '+ New Lab Order' button

**From Clinical Encounter:**
1. During patient visit/note documentation
2. Click 'Order Labs' in encounter toolbar
3. Patient context auto-populated

**Creating Lab Order - 6 Steps:**

**STEP 1: Basic Information**
• Patient (pre-populated from context)
• Ordering Provider (usually current user)
• Order Date (defaults to today)
• Priority (Routine, STAT, ASAP)
• Clinical Indication (ICD-10 diagnosis - REQUIRED)

**STEP 2: Select Lab Tests (CPT Codes)**
**NEW:** Multi-select interface for multiple tests!

1. Click 'Select Tests' field
2. Dropdown shows 80+ common tests organized by category:

**Categories:**
🩸 Hematology - CBC (85025), CBC with Diff (85027), Platelet Count
🧬 Chemistry - BMP (80048), CMP (80053), Glucose (82947)
💉 Coagulation - PT/INR (85610), PTT (85730), D-Dimer
🧪 Lipids - Lipid Panel (80061), Cholesterol, Triglycerides
🔬 Microbiology - Urinalysis (81001), Urine Culture (87086)
💊 Therapeutic - Drug levels (Digoxin, Theophylline)
🩺 Endocrine - TSH (84443), T4 (84439), A1C (83036)
🧫 Immunology - ANA (86038), RF (86431), CRP (86140)

3. Type to search by test name or CPT code
4. Click to select - tests appear as chips/tags
5. Click X on chip to remove test
6. Selected tests show with CPT codes

**Quick Panels:** Select panel to get multiple tests at once
• Basic Metabolic Panel = 8 individual tests
• Comprehensive Metabolic Panel = 14 tests
• Lipid Panel = 4 tests

**STEP 3: Collection Details**
• Collection Method (In-Clinic, At Laboratory, Home Collection)
• **NEW:** Scheduled Date/Time (supports future dates!)
• Fasting Required (toggle Yes/No)
• Fasting Duration (8, 10, or 12 hours)
• Specimen Type (Blood, Urine, Stool, Throat Swab, etc.)

**NEW: Recurring Orders**
For chronic condition monitoring:
1. Toggle 'Recurring Order' switch
2. Select frequency:
   • Daily
   • Weekly (specify day)
   • Bi-weekly
   • Monthly (specify day of month)
   • Quarterly
   • Custom interval
3. Set start date and end date (or # of occurrences)
4. System auto-generates future orders

**Use Cases for Recurring:**
• Monthly INR for warfarin patients
• Quarterly A1C for diabetic patients
• Weekly drug levels for specific medications

**STEP 4: Laboratory Selection**
1. Preferred Lab (patient's preferred if on file)
2. Search by name, location, specialty
3. In-Network Labs (filter by patient insurance)
4. Verify lab performs ordered tests

**STEP 5: Results Distribution**
**NEW:** Multi-select recipients!
Select who receives results:
• Ordering Provider (auto-selected)
• Primary Care Physician
• Specialist (from care team)
• Patient Portal (auto-posts when ready)
• Other Provider (search and add)

**STEP 6: Review and Submit**
1. Review all order details
2. Verify tests and CPT codes
3. Confirm laboratory and collection method
4. Check result recipients
5. Click 'Submit Order'

**After Submission:**
• Order transmitted electronically to lab
• Requisition form generated
• Patient receives instructions (portal/email/SMS)
• Order appears in pending labs list

**Enhanced Print Functionality:**

**Print Options:**
1. After creating order, click 'Print'
2. Choose format:
   • Full Requisition - Complete form with all details
   • Patient Instructions - Prep instructions only
   • Both - Requisition + instructions on separate pages
3. Preview before printing
4. Print directly or save as PDF

**Requisition Includes:**
• Patient demographics and insurance
• All ordered tests with CPT codes
• ICD-10 diagnosis codes
• Provider information and signature
• Collection instructions
• Laboratory barcode

**Managing Lab Orders:**

**Status Tracking:**
• Pending - Order created, awaiting collection
• Scheduled - Collection appointment scheduled
• Collected - Specimen collected, sent to lab
• In Progress - Lab processing tests
• Partial Results - Some results available
• Completed - All results received
• Cancelled - Order cancelled before collection

**Cancelling Orders:**
1. Go to Patient Chart > Laboratory
2. Find pending order
3. Click 'Cancel Order'
4. Select reason and add notes
5. Confirm cancellation
Note: Can only cancel before specimen collection

**Viewing Results:**
1. System notification for new results
2. Go to Patient Chart > Laboratory
3. Click completed order
4. Review results panel:
   • Test name and value
   • Reference range
   • Abnormal flag (H, L, Critical)
   • Result date/time
   • Performing lab

**Abnormal Results:**
🔴 Critical (H/L) - Red text, immediate attention
🟡 Abnormal - Yellow background, outside range
⚪ Normal - Standard display, within range

**Critical Values:** Trigger immediate alerts via SMS, email, system notification. Must acknowledge and document follow-up.

**Documenting Review:**
1. Click 'Sign Results'
2. Add interpretation notes
3. Document follow-up plan:
   • No action needed
   • Retest scheduled
   • Treatment adjustment
   • Specialist referral
   • Patient notified
4. Apply electronic signature

**Best Practices:**
• Always include diagnosis for insurance approval
• Use panels when appropriate to reduce costs
• Check for duplicates before ordering
• Set correct priority (reserve STAT for emergencies)
• Verify fasting requirements
• Use recurring orders for chronic monitoring
• Sign all results promptly
• Document action on abnormal results
• Notify patients of results timely

articles.title: Zoom Integration Guide
articles.summary:
Add, use, and remove the Zoom app for telehealth sessions

Step-by-step guide covering OAuth setup, scheduling and starting video sessions, cloud recording, and how to disconnect and delete Zoom data.
articles.content:
**Adding the Zoom App:**

Prerequisites:
• Active AureonCare Administrator account
• Zoom account (Pro, Business, or higher)
• Pop-ups allowed in your browser

Steps:
1. Log in and go to Settings > Integrations
2. Find the Zoom card under Telehealth Providers
3. Click Connect Zoom
4. Sign in to Zoom and click Allow
5. Zoom card shows Connected badge when done
6. Optionally click Test Connection to verify

Permissions granted: meeting:write, meeting:read, recording:read, user:read

**Usage:**

Schedule a Telehealth Appointment:
• Go to Practice Management > Appointments
• Create a new appointment with type Telehealth
• AureonCare auto-creates a Zoom meeting and sends the patient a join link

Start a Session (Provider):
• Open the appointment and click Start Video Consultation
• Allow camera and microphone when prompted
• The Zoom session opens inside AureonCare

articles.title: Claims Management
articles.summary:
Create and submit insurance claims electronically

Submit claims to insurance payers with real-time eligibility verification and status tracking.
articles.content:
**Creating Insurance Claims:**

**Accessing Claims:**
1. Go to Revenue Cycle Management module
2. Click 'Claims' tab
3. Click '+ New Claim' button

**Automatic Claim Generation:**
Claims auto-generate from:
• Completed appointments
• Signed clinical encounter notes
• Procedures performed
• Services rendered

System automatically:
• Links diagnosis codes (ICD-10)
• Links procedure codes (CPT)
• Pulls patient insurance information
• Calculates charges
• Validates claim data

**Manual Claim Creation:**

Step 1: Patient Selection
• Search by name or MRN
• System displays active insurance
• Verify coverage is active

Step 2: Service Information
• Date of Service (DOS)
• Place of Service (POS code)
• Type of Service
• Rendering Provider
• Referring Provider (if applicable)

Step 3: Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10)
• Primary diagnosis (required)
• Secondary diagnoses (up to 11)
• Diagnosis pointer for each procedure
• Search by code or description

Step 4: Procedure Codes (CPT/HCPCS)
For each service:
• CPT/HCPCS code
• Modifiers (if applicable)
• Units/quantity
• Charge amount
• Diagnosis pointer (links to ICD-10)

**Common CPT Codes:**
• 99213 - Established patient office visit (15 min)
• 99214 - Established patient office visit (25 min)
• 99203 - New patient office visit (30 min)
• 99204 - New patient office visit (45 min)
• 99396 - Preventive visit, established

Step 5: Review and Validate
System checks:
• Coverage verification
• Medical necessity (diagnosis supports procedure)
• Duplicate claim detection
• Missing required fields
• Coding errors

**Real-Time Eligibility Verification:**
1. Click 'Verify Coverage' button
2. System contacts payer in real-time
3. Returns:
   • Active/Inactive status
   • Deductible met/remaining
   • Co-pay amount
   • Co-insurance percentage
   • Out-of-pocket max
   • Prior authorization requirements

**Submitting Claims:**

**Electronic Submission (837):**
1. Review claim details
2. Click 'Submit Electronically'
3. Claim sent via clearinghouse
4. Receive acknowledgement (999/997)
5. Status updates automatically

**Paper Submission (CMS-1500):**
1. Click 'Print CMS-1500'
2. Review form for accuracy
3. Print and sign
4. Mail to payer address
5. Manually track status

**Claim Status Tracking:**

• Draft - Claim created, not submitted
• Ready to Submit - Validated, awaiting submission
• Submitted - Sent to payer
• Acknowledged - Payer received claim
• In Process - Payer processing claim
• Accepted - Claim approved for payment
• Paid - Payment received (EOB posted)
• Denied - Claim rejected by payer
• Appealed - Denial appealed
• Closed - Claim finalized

**Claim Denials:**

Common Denial Reasons:
• Coverage terminated
• Services not covered
• Missing/invalid diagnosis code
• Medical necessity not met
• Timely filing limit exceeded
• Duplicate claim
• Incorrect patient information

**Handling Denials:**
1. Click denied claim
2. Review denial reason code
3. Check EOB/remittance advice
4. Determine action:
   • Correct and resubmit
   • Appeal with documentation
   • Write off as adjustment
   • Bill patient (if applicable)

**Corrected Claims:**
1. Open denied claim
2. Click 'Create Corrected Claim'
3. Update incorrect information
4. Mark as 'Corrected Claim' (Claim Frequency 7)
5. Reference original claim number (ICN)
6. Resubmit

**Appeals Process:**
1. Click 'Appeal Denial'
2. Select appeal level (1st, 2nd, 3rd)
3. Upload supporting documents:
   • Clinical notes
   • Lab results
   • Medical necessity letter
   • Peer-reviewed articles
4. Write appeal letter
5. Submit appeal
6. Track appeal status

**Payment Posting (EOB/ERA):**

When payment received:
1. System receives ERA (Electronic Remittance)
2. Or manually enter EOB (Explanation of Benefits)
3. Post payment:
   • Amount paid by insurance
   • Patient responsibility
   • Adjustments/contractual write-offs
   • Denial amounts
4. System updates:
   • Patient account balance
   • Claim status to 'Paid'
   • Generates patient statement if balance due

**Batch Claims Processing:**

1. Go to Claims > Batch Processing
2. Filter claims:
   • Date range
   • Payer
   • Provider
   • Status (Ready to Submit)
3. Select multiple claims
4. Bulk actions:
   • Submit all
   • Validate all
   • Export to file
   • Print batch

**Claims Reporting:**

**Available Reports:**
• Claims Aging (by payer, provider)
• Denial Rate Analysis
• Days in A/R
• Clean Claim Rate
• Payment by Payer
• Top Denial Reasons
• Revenue by CPT Code

**Best Practices:**
• Verify insurance before each visit
• Submit claims within 24-48 hours
• Review claims for accuracy before submission
• Monitor aging reports weekly
• Follow up on claims >30 days
• Appeal valid denials promptly
• Document all payer communications
• Keep CPT and ICD-10 codes current
• Train staff on coding updates
• Use correct modifiers
• Link appropriate diagnoses to procedures
• Check timely filing limits by payer

**Six Core Tabs:**

1. **Overview** – KPI cards and account balance summary

articles.title: Journal Entries
articles.summary:
Record and review double-entry journal entries

Every transaction requires balanced debits and credits. System auto-generates entries for AR, AP, and reconciliation; manual entries can also be created.
articles.content:
**Journal Entries:**

Journal entries are the core of double-entry bookkeeping. Every financial transaction must have equal debits and credits.

**Accessing Journal Entries:**
1. Go to Accounts module
2. Click 'Journal Entries' tab
3. All entries are listed chronologically

**Creating a Manual Journal Entry:**
1. Click '+ New Journal Entry'
2. Fill in header:
   • Entry Date
   • Description (what this entry records)
   • Entry Type (manual, adjustment, closing)
   • Reference Number (optional)
3. Add journal lines:
   • Select Account
   • Choose Debit or Credit
   • Enter Amount
   • Add line description (optional)
4. Add more lines as needed (minimum 2)
5. Verify the entry is Balanced (Debits = Credits)
6. Click 'Create Entry'

**Balanced Entries:**
The form shows running totals:
• Total Debits
• Total Credits
• Balance indicator (green = balanced, red = not balanced)

You cannot save an unbalanced entry.

**Common Journal Entry Types:**

**Revenue Recording:**
Debit: Accounts Receivable
Credit: Patient Services Revenue

**Cash Receipt:**
Debit: Cash/Bank Account
Credit: Accounts Receivable

**Expense Payment:**
Debit: Expense Account
Credit: Cash/Bank Account

**Payroll:**
Debit: Payroll Expense
Credit: Cash/Bank Account

**Depreciation:**
Debit: Depreciation Expense
Credit: Accumulated Depreciation

**Viewing Journal Entries:**
• Date, description, entry type, and totals shown in list
• Click any entry to view all lines
• Filter by date range, entry type, or account
• Export to CSV/Excel

**Voiding Entries:**
Never delete a journal entry — void it instead:
1. Open the journal entry
2. Click 'Void Entry'
3. Add reason for void
4. System creates a reversing entry automatically
5. Both original and void entries remain in audit trail

**Auto-Generated Entries:**
The system automatically creates journal entries when:
• An AR record is created (debit AR, credit Revenue)
• An AP invoice is entered (debit Expense, credit AP)
• A payment is received (debit Cash, credit AR)
• A payment is made (debit AP, credit Cash)
• A reconciliation is completed

**Best Practices:**
• Include clear, descriptive entry descriptions
• Reference source documents (invoice #, receipt #)
• Review entries for accuracy before month-end
• Never delete entries — always void
• Post entries in the correct accounting period
• Reconcile accounts after posting entries

articles.title: Bank Reconciliation
articles.summary:
Reconcile your bank and credit card statements with your books

Match bank statement transactions against your accounting records to identify discrepancies and ensure accuracy.
articles.content:
**Bank Reconciliation:**

Reconciliation verifies that your accounting records match your actual bank or credit card statements.

**Accessing Reconciliation:**
1. Go to Accounts module
2. Click 'Reconciliation' tab
3. All reconciliation records are listed

**Creating a Reconciliation:**
1. Click '+ New Reconciliation'
2. Fill in:
   • Account (bank or credit card account)
   • Reconciliation Type (Bank, Credit Card, Other)
   • Period Start Date
   • Period End Date
   • Statement Balance (from your bank statement)
   • Notes
3. Save

**Reconciliation Status:**
• In Progress – Still being worked on
• Balanced – Statement balance matches system balance
• Discrepancy – Difference found between statement and books
• Completed – Reconciliation finalized

**Resolving Discrepancies:**
If Statement Balance ≠ System Balance:
1. Check for transactions in the bank not in your books (add journal entry)
2. Check for transactions in your books not on the statement (timing difference)
3. Look for transposition errors or duplicate entries
4. Check for bank fees or interest not yet recorded

**Best Practices:**
• Reconcile every account monthly
• Use bank statement end date as the reconciliation period end
• Investigate all discrepancies — never force-balance
• Complete reconciliation within 10 days of statement receipt
• Keep copies of bank statements on file

articles.title: Financial Statements
articles.summary:
Generate income statements, balance sheets, and trial balances

articles.content:
**Financial Statements:**

Generate standard financial reports from your accounting data.

**Accessing Statements:**
1. Go to Accounts module

**Available Statement Types:**

**Income Statement (Profit & Loss):**
Shows revenue, expenses, and net income for a period

• Expenses by category
• Gross Profit
• Net Income/Loss

**Balance Sheet:**
Snapshot of financial position at a specific date
• Assets (current and non-current)
• Liabilities (current and long-term)
• Equity
• Must balance: Assets = Liabilities + Equity

**Trial Balance:**
List of all accounts with debit and credit balances
• Verifies books are in balance
• Used to prepare other statements
• Adjusted trial balance includes adjusting entries

**Statement of Cash Flows:**
Shows cash inflows and outflows
• Operating activities
• Investing activities
• Financing activities

**Generating a Statement:**
1. Select statement type
2. Set the period (date range)
3. Click 'Generate'
4. Review on screen
5. Export as PDF or CSV

**Best Practices:**
• Generate statements at month-end and year-end
• Compare current period to prior period
• Share income statement with practice leadership monthly
• Use trial balance to verify books before period close
• Keep statements for at least 7 years

articles.title: Managing Inventory Items
articles.summary:
Add, edit, and manage items in your inventory catalog

Each item tracks name, SKU, category, supplier, unit cost, current stock, reorder level, and expiry date.
articles.content:
**Managing Inventory Items:**

**Accessing Items:**
1. Go to Inventory module
2. Click 'Items' tab
3. All items listed with current stock, cost, and status

**Adding a New Item:**
1. Click '+ New Item'
2. Fill in required fields:
   • Item Name
   • SKU / Item Code (unique identifier)
   • Category
   • Unit of Measure (each, box, ml, mg, etc.)
   • Unit Cost
   • Reorder Level (minimum stock before alert triggers)
   • Reorder Quantity (how much to order when restocking)
3. Optional fields:
   • Description
   • Supplier (preferred supplier)
   • Barcode
   • Expiry Date
   • Storage Location
   • Notes
4. Save

**Item Status:**
• Active – In use, appears in stock movements
• Inactive – Discontinued, hidden from stock forms
• Low Stock – Current stock ≤ Reorder Level (highlighted)
• Out of Stock – Current stock = 0 (flagged)

**Editing Items:**
1. Click item name or edit icon
2. Update fields
3. Save

Note: Changing Unit Cost affects future valuation but not historical records.

**Low Stock Alerts:**
When current stock ≤ reorder level:
• Item highlighted in the list
• Low Stock count shown on Overview card
• Use this to trigger purchase orders

**Item Search and Filter:**
• Search by name, SKU, or barcode
• Filter by category, supplier, status
• Sort by name, stock level, cost, or expiry date

articles.summary:
Record all stock in and out movements to maintain accurate inventory

articles.content:
**Stock Movements:**

Every change in stock quantity must be recorded as a movement to maintain accurate inventory levels.

**Accessing Stock Movements:**
1. Go to Inventory module
2. Click 'Stock' tab
3. All movement history is listed

**Movement Types:**

**Receive:**
Add stock when shipment arrives
• Select item
• Enter quantity received
• Enter unit cost (if different from item default)
• Add reference (PO number, delivery note)
• Add notes

**Dispense:**
Remove stock when used in patient care
• Select item
• Enter quantity dispensed
• Link to patient or department
• Add notes

**Adjust:**
Correct stock after a count discrepancy
• Select item
• Enter adjustment quantity (positive or negative)
• Add reason (damaged, expired, count correction)

**Transfer:**
Move stock between locations or departments
• Select item
• Enter quantity
• Specify from/to location

**Creating a Stock Movement:**
1. Click '+ New Movement'
2. Select Movement Type
3. Select Item (search by name or SKU)
4. Enter Quantity
5. Add Reference and Notes
6. Save

Stock levels update immediately. The system prevents stock from going below zero on dispense movements.

**Movement History:**
• Full audit trail of all movements
• Filter by item, movement type, date range, or user
• Export movement history for audits
• Each movement shows who created it and when

**Best Practices:**
• Record movements as they happen — don't batch
• Always reference the PO or delivery note when receiving
• Conduct monthly stock counts and adjust for discrepancies
• Investigate all negative adjustments
• Use consistent movement types for reporting accuracy

articles.title: Purchase Orders
articles.summary:

articles.content:
**Purchase Orders (PO):**

Purchase orders formalize your requests to suppliers and enable accurate receiving.

**Accessing Purchase Orders:**
1. Go to Inventory module
2. Click 'Purchase Orders' tab
3. All POs listed with status and total value

**Creating a Purchase Order:**
1. Click '+ New PO'
2. Select Supplier
3. Set Order Date and Expected Delivery Date
4. Add line items:
   • Select Item
   • Enter Quantity Ordered
   • Confirm Unit Cost
   • Line total auto-calculated
5. Add more lines as needed
6. Review Order Total
7. Add Notes (special instructions, delivery notes)
8. Save

**PO Status Workflow:**
• Draft – PO created, not yet sent
• Submitted – PO sent to supplier
• Approved – Supplier confirmed the order
• Partially Received – Some items received
• Received – All items received
• Cancelled – PO cancelled

**Receiving a Purchase Order:**
When items arrive:
1. Find the PO in the list
2. Click 'Receive'
3. For each line, enter quantity actually received
4. Confirm unit costs match invoice
5. Click 'Confirm Receipt'
6. System automatically creates stock movement (Receive) for all items
7. Stock levels update immediately

**Partial Receipts:**
If only some items arrive:
1. Enter actual quantities received for each line
2. Leave undelivered lines at 0 or partial quantity
3. PO status changes to 'Partially Received'
4. Receive remaining items when they arrive

**PO Total:**
Order total displayed in the currency from your Clinic Settings. All line totals auto-calculate.

**Best Practices:**
• Create a PO before ordering from any supplier
• Reference PO number in all supplier communications
• Match received goods to PO before accepting delivery
• Record partial receipts immediately
• Review open POs weekly for overdue deliveries
• Cancel POs for items no longer needed
